title: Map every executable interlocking guard path to exactly one train route or classify it as structural residual

facts.note: The only enforcement trigger: the validator runs at CONFIRM and is confirm-blocking; the harness must supply the phase. The validation subject is each interlocking in the plan (subject_kind: interlocking), changed or not. Identifying interlocking validation subjects is not a file-kind fact; it needs a new subject observer (the plan's interlocking subjects as seen by the coverage validator).

fires: At CONFIRM, an interlocking (new, edited or unchanged) has an executable guard path with no train route and no explicit structural-residual classification.
At CONFIRM, an executable guard path that is not explicitly classified as structural residual is mapped to two or more train routes.
At CONFIRM, after a train route was removed from the plan, an executable guard path it covered is left unmapped and not classified as structural residual.
doesNotFire: Any phase other than CONFIRM (e.g. while the planner is still drafting guards or routes); the check is enforced only at CONFIRM.
An executable guard path explicitly classified as structural residual.
Every executable guard path in the interlocking maps to exactly one train route.
Plans that contain no interlocking subject.
Non-executable content in an interlocking (not a guard path).

given: A plan containing an interlocking with executable guard paths and the train routes projected from it
when: The plan reaches CONFIRM (whether or not the interlocking was changed)
then: Every executable guard path in the interlocking maps to exactly one train route, unless it is explicitly classified as structural residual.
prefer: For each executable guard path, name the single train route that carries it, so the plan already satisfies the CONFIRM check.
When a guard path truly belongs to no route, mark it explicitly as structural residual instead of leaving it unmapped.
avoid: Leaving an executable guard path with no route and no explicit structural-residual classification.
Mapping a guard path that is not explicitly classified as structural residual to several routes.
Classifying routable guard paths as structural residual just to silence the coverage check.
unless: The guard path is explicitly classified as structural residual.
why: A guard path with no train route is a control path no train exercises, and one claimed by several routes has ambiguous ownership; exactly-one coverage keeps the train projection faithful to the interlocking.
evidence: Coverage validator (projection_covers_source) passes for every interlocking subject at CONFIRM.
On failure, the failure evidence carries the fields interlocking_id, guard_id, route_id and coverage_status.
Every executable guard path maps to exactly one train route or is explicitly classified as structural residual.
verifier_detail: Phase: CONFIRM (only enforcement point); enforcement: confirm-blocking; subject_kind: interlocking (all interlockings in the plan, changed or unchanged).

Term guard_coverage: each executable guard path maps to exactly one route, or is explicitly classified as a structural residual. For paths not explicitly classified as structural residual: zero routes = fail; two or more routes = fail. Paths explicitly classified as structural residual are exempt from the exactly-one requirement.
Failure evidence fields: interlocking_id, guard_id, route_id, coverage_status.
